title: Ankhorage Social
summary: Provides provider-neutral capability, media-preflight, and idempotent execution boundaries for social actions.
purpose: Give independently released applications a typed social-action dispatch boundary without coupling workflows to Connection, Flow, OAuth, credential storage, or provider SDKs.
responsibilities: Publish typed commands, operation-target receipts, and generic authorization, media, and provider ports for social actions.
Preflight provider account and destination capabilities, content formats, media metadata, and current trusted scopes.
Reconcile stable operation keys before one provider execution attempt without persisting provider state.
boundaries: Does not own Connection, Flow, OAuth, credential storage, media upload, provider SDK authentication, or provider-specific payloads.
Does not execute Flow orchestration or persist action state, idempotency records, or receipts.
Does not require consumers to use unpublished sibling sources or an Ankhorage application.
audience: Application authors dispatching social actions through provider adapters.
Adapter authors implementing trusted authorization, media preflight, and provider boundaries for social platforms.
useCases: Dispatch an authorized publish, comment, reply, reaction, or repost action to a matching provider adapter.
Reject malformed, unauthorized, mismatched, unsupported, unpreflighted, or ambiguous actions before provider execution.

architecture.role: Provider-neutral social action library with explicit authorization, media preflight, and provider ports.
invariants: Social action dispatch remains independent from Connection, Flow, OAuth, credential storage, media upload, and provider SDKs.
Trusted authorization binds the exact operation, tenant, actor, and target before every provider effect.
Provider adapters own platform authentication, durable idempotency, reconciliation, and receipt persistence.
Consumers use the published package entrypoint and declared dependencies.

limitations: Provider capabilities, authorization decisions, media source validation, idempotency guarantees, and receipts depend on caller-supplied adapters.
Social never claims exactly-once delivery and fails closed for ambiguous reconciliation or execution outcomes.
